findings.element: Bulk action bar → "↩ Rollback" confirmation dialog
findings.finding: The Rollback confirmation is the only destructive action on the page that tells me something "will be deleted" without also telling me it can be undone, while the neighbouring Archive and Cancel dialogs both reassure me explicitly.
findings.user_impact: I cancel out of the dialog and leave the failed transactions untouched, because deleting records in my accounting software sounds like something my accountant will find and I will not be able to fix.
findings.suggested_fix: Add a recovery sentence and keep the canonical verb: "Rollback 1 transaction? The entries created in your books will be removed. The transaction stays in Synder and you can sync it again."

evidence.quote: Rollback 1 transaction? The records created in your accounting platform will be deleted.
evidence.source: vocabulary.md → UI Words: "Rollback (buttons/statuses; "rolled back" in past tense)" — the term is canonical, so this is a missing-reassurance finding, not a rename; contrast the Archive dialog's "but can be restored later."

findings.element: Table → "Sync status" badge "Not parsed" on row po_1TKnR6E4pygkgelb8eE1Ff03, under the "Needs attention" tab
findings.finding: "Not parsed" is a software word, not a business word, and nothing on the screen explains it — the only tooltip on the page is on the column header and just says the status describes my accounting system.
findings.user_impact: I am told this row needs my attention but cannot tell whether Synder failed, my Stripe data is broken, or I did something wrong, so I click "Retry" hoping it goes away and give up when it does not.
findings.suggested_fix: Give each status a plain-language explanation on hover or in a "what's this?" popover — for this one: "Synder couldn't read this transaction's details. Nothing was sent to your books."

evidence.source: vocabulary.md → Statuses → Platform Transactions lists "Not parsed" as canonical, so the fix is an added explanation; unexplained jargon otherwise (the only hint on the list page is title="Status of this transaction in your accounting system")

findings.element: Status segment tab "Successful" → rows badged "Excluded from sync" and "Skipped"
findings.finding: The "Successful" tab lists transactions whose own status says they were never synced, so the tab label and the row contradict each other on the one question I actually care about.
findings.user_impact: I cannot answer "is this sale in my books or not?", so I stop trusting the counts and either re-sync rows that were deliberately excluded or ask my accountant to check the whole list manually.
findings.suggested_fix: Rename the group to something that covers both outcomes, e.g. "Completed", and add hover text on these two statuses: "Deliberately not sent to your books — no action needed."

evidence.source: vocabulary.md → Statuses → Platform Transactions lists "Excluded from sync" and "Skipped" as canonical status names; the "Successful" group label is prototype copy, not vocabulary.md, so the group name is the changeable half

gaps: Row "Actions" verbs (Retry / Sync / View sync) all navigate to the transaction detail page, which was not exercised — I cannot tell whether "Retry" ever explains what failed or what retrying will do, which is where the CLR-2 explanation would most plausibly already live.

"Import historical data" was clicked and opened no dialog, so the biggest first-timer anxiety on this screen — "will importing history duplicate the transactions I already have?" — has no observable copy to judge.
Bulk "⟳ Sync now" only produced "Syncing 1 transaction…"; no success or failure message was reached, so I cannot judge whether the user is told what landed in their books.
Export to CSV menu items are inert, so no copy exists for what a first-timer would hand to their accountant.
